entries.text: ORDER: The Court intimates no views on the merits of Petitioner's claims but concludes, given (among other things) the nature of those claims, that the case would benefit from pro bono counsel. Accordingly, the Clerk of Court is directed to se ek pro bono counsel for Petitioner. See Hodge v. Police Officers, 802 F.2d 58, 60 (2d Cir. 1986). The Court requests that the Petitioner respond promptly to any outreach by a volunteer lawyer seeking to discuss possible pro bono representation. Petit ioner should promptly advise the Court if she has an objection to the Court seeking pro bono representation. Unless and until pro bono counsel enters a notice of appearance on behalf of Petitioner, she remains pro se and should be prepared to proceed with the case pro se. The Clerk of Court is directed to mail a copy of this Order to Petitioner. SO ORDERED. (Signed by Judge Jesse M. Furman on 9/16/2026) (ar) Order
